$comment: DRAFT ledger for issue #60, one director only (Satyajit Ray). Same schema as essential10-example.json (schemaVersion 1) with additive fields: format, tmdbYear, sightAndSound2022, rt.reason, rt.alternateCut. Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Owner decision 2026-11-13: films are ranked by IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes scores. Each film is ranked within this list by IMDb rating and by Tomatometer (ties share the average rank); the two ranks are averaged (ranks, never the raw scores); ties are broken by higher IMDb rating, then more IMDb votes. A Tomatometer with fewer than 10 reviews or no value is ignored and that film is ranked by IMDb alone (flagged rtUsed:false). The film selection is unchanged from the editorial research list; editorialRank keeps the earlier order. Scores are read online and dated, never estimated.

imdb.source: IMDb non-commercial dataset title.ratings.tsv.gz (averageRating, numVotes), matched on IMDb title id; title ids found through title.crew.tsv.gz (director nconst) and cross-checked against TMDB by title, year and runtime
imdb.note: Live IMDb title pages were attempted first and did not return a usable page to an automated request (an empty response, not a human-readable page), so ratings come from the official daily dataset instead; this is the same fallback as the Kurosawa example. The dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see licensing caveats in ESSENTIAL_10_EXAMPLE.md.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer (scorePercent) and critic review count (reviewCount) read from the page's embedded data
rt.note: Read directly from each film's rottentomatoes.com page with a command-line fetch, one request per page. Percentages and counts are live and change; treat as a dated snapshot. Where a page shows fewer than about 5 reviews no Tomatometer is published and the value is null.

sightAndSound.source: BFI, The Greatest Films of All Time (2022 Sight and Sound poll), positions as listed on the page
sightAndSound.note: The page text was read in two halves; ranks 49-50 and the very bottom of the list were not visible in the extracted text. A film shown without a position was not seen in the portions read; that is not proof it is absent. '=' marks a tie. The page does not state 'critics' poll' in the extracted text, so the figure is labelled 'the 2022 Sight and Sound poll'.

films.title: Nayak
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).
films.rationale: A film star and a journalist on an overnight train; a near two-hander played largely in one confined setting, with Uttam Kumar in the lead; RT 100% but from only 10 reviews.

films.title: The World of Apu
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).

rt.rtYearNote: RT page shows a later US release year (1960).

films.rationale: The close of the Apu trilogy and the highest IMDb rating in the ten (8.4); marriage, fatherhood and grief told as Apu's coming-of-age ends.

films.title: Mahanagar
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A Calcutta housewife takes a job and changes her household; an early film about women at work, with the Silver Bear for Best Director at Berlin 1964.

films.title: Pather Panchali
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: His first film, made on a tiny budget with largely non-professional actors, that opened Indian cinema to the world; 98% from 82 reviews on RT and the highest-placed Ray in the 2022 Sight and Sound poll (35th).

films.title: Days and Nights in the Forest
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: Four Calcutta friends on a forest holiday, an ensemble comedy of manners with 100% on RT from 23 reviews and a distinct late-period register.

films.title: Aparajito
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: The middle of the trilogy, following Apu from Benares to Calcutta; Golden Lion at Venice 1957, which confirmed his international standing.

films.title: The Music Room
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).

rt.rtYearNote: RT page is titled 'Jalsaghar' and shows 1960.

films.rationale: A decaying zamindar's last devotion to music, with the film's music and décor doing the dramatic work; 100% on RT from 23 reviews.

films.title: Devi
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A young wife is declared a goddess by her father-in-law, a quiet study of belief and its cost; 100% on RT from 15 reviews.

films.title: Charulata
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A bored wife in 1879 Calcutta and her husband's cousin, filmed with a restraint and fluid camera work that make it his most polished chamber piece; Silver Bear for Best Director at Berlin 1965.

films.title: Distant Thunder
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).

rt.rtYearNote: RT shows 100% from only 5 reviews: not a usable sample.

films.rationale: The 1943 Bengal famine seen from one village, in colour; winner of the Golden Bear at Berlin 1973. The thinnest evidence in the ten (1,918 IMDb votes, 5 RT reviews), kept as the closest call (see below).

nearMisses.title: Teen Kanya (Three Daughters)
nearMisses.reason: Three Tagore stories; IMDb 7.9 from 1,868 votes, not stronger than Distant Thunder on available evidence.

nearMisses.title: The Adventures of Goopy and Bagha
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 8.6 from 6,134 votes but only 4 RT reviews and a children's fantasy register; first reserve for a tenth place.

nearMisses.title: The Home and the World
nearMisses.reason: RT 100% from 12 reviews and a major literary adaptation; very close to Distant Thunder.

nearMisses.title: The Adversary (Pratidwandi)
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 8.1 from 2,147 votes; the first of the Calcutta trilogy.

nearMisses.title: Jana Aranya (The Middleman)
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 8.3 from 2,028 votes; RT 88% from 8 reviews (listed as 'The Masses' Music').

nearMisses.title: The Chess Players
nearMisses.reason: His Hindi-language feature, 100% from 10 reviews; outside his core Bengali body of work.

unverified: Evidence is thin for most of the ten (see above). Distant Thunder's 100% on RT is from 5 reviews and should not be treated as a Tomatometer in any display.
IMDb ids were matched by title, year and runtime; The Music Room is 100 minutes on TMDB and 95 on IMDb, Devi 99 and 99, all in a plausible range.
RT pages for Devi and Distant Thunder have US re-release years; the ledger uses the original release year.

The Berlin awards were verified in a web search (Wikipedia lists and satyajitray.org); a second search found one source dating Charulata's Silver Bear to 1964, the others to 1965. The ledger says 1965.
Ray's Golden Lion for Aparajito (Venice 1957) and the Golden Bear for Distant Thunder (Berlin 1973) were confirmed in the same search.
